description: Audit-lane owned registry for Tier-A accepted non-axiom premise handling. As of 2026-05-26, the registry distinguishes three input categories: (1) admitted derivation targets (genuine framework-specific gaps the framework can attempt to close — currently P1, AC_phi_lambda, theta); (2) empirical anchors (single empirical numbers that fix dimensionful scales — currently S, reclassified 2026-05-26 from ambiguous not_a_node tracking, analog of SM Higgs VEV v=246 GeV and GR G_Newton); (3) conventions (Y0 and g0, vacuous rescaling choices, excluded from admission count). Derivation targets are accepted as chain-satisfying premises at the bounded tier, so a clean row depending on one resolves to retained_bounded rather than retained_pending_chain; when a target is derived, remove its entry and compute_effective_status will auto-cascade dependents toward unbounded retained status when otherwise eligible. Empirical anchors are NOT derivation targets in the same sense; they are honest external inputs (single dimensionful number per theory) shared with every physics theory (e.g., SM v=246 GeV, GR G_Newton). The framework's advantage is reducing many SM dimensionful parameters to a single empirical anchor via substrate-derived ratios. This registry is distinct from axiom_premise_nodes.json and from standard textbook theorems, which must earn retained-grade inline. Human-readable registry: docs/ADMITTED_INPUT_REGISTRY_TIER_A_NOTE_2026-05-23.md.

observable_principle_from_axiom_note.label: P1
observable_principle_from_axiom_note.statement: scalar observables are additive over independent subsystems; forces W = log|det(D+J)|

staggered_dirac_realization_gate_note_20.label: AC_phi_lambda
staggered_dirac_realization_gate_note_20.statement: generation mass-pattern input: the C_3-breaking phase/orientation plus the abstract-sector to physical-species bridge; bare e/mu/tau naming is a convention, not a derivation target
staggered_dirac_realization_gate_note_20.class: discrete flavor input with labeling convention stripped

strong_cp_theta_zero_note.label: theta
strong_cp_theta_zero_note.statement: the QCD vacuum angle theta = 0 (strong-CP); also unsolved in the Standard Model

S.label: absolute scale
S.statement: one empirical scale-setting number (match a single observable to fix a); the unit choice itself is vacuous, and S is pervasive with no single citeable parent row
S.leverage: pervasive — fixes the overall lattice spacing a > 0 that propagates everywhere
S.reclassification_basis: Reclassified 2026-05-26 from not_a_node (ambiguous tracking) to formal empirical_anchor category. The framework's substrate provides lattice spacing a > 0 as a free parameter; no natural scale-setting mechanism is internal to the substrate. The 3-no-go portfolio (planck-related foreclosures) confirms S is irreducible to substrate primitives without external empirical input — this is a CONVERGENT FORECLOSURE pattern (3 independent attempts all failing), mirroring the multi-witness pattern used for AC_phi_lambda (positive, PR #1965) and P1 (negative, PR #1983). S is the framework's analog of SM Higgs VEV v=246 GeV (fixing electroweak mass scale) and GR Newton constant G_N (fixing gravitational coupling scale). Every physics theory has exactly this kind of single empirical anchor; the framework's strength is reducing SM's ~19 free parameters to ~1 (S) after substrate-derived structure is accounted for.

SM_higgs_vev.role: fixes electroweak mass scale (M_W = gv/2, m_f = y_f v / sqrt(2))
SM_higgs_vev.derivability_in_SM: empirical anchor; v itself is not derived from anything more fundamental in the SM
SM_higgs_vev.parallel_to_S: Both are single dimensionful numbers fixed by one experimental measurement; both are required external inputs to make dimensionful predictions

GR_G_newton.role: fixes gravitational coupling scale and Planck mass M_Pl = (hbar c / G_N)^{1/2}
GR_G_newton.derivability_in_GR: empirical anchor; G_N itself is not derived from anything more fundamental in GR
GR_G_newton.parallel_to_S: Both fix the overall dimensionful scale of the theory; both are necessarily external

comparison_to_other_theories.framework_advantage: After S is fixed, the framework derives ALL OTHER SM dimensionful parameters from substrate primitives: mass ratios (Koide closure for charged leptons), hypercharge ratios (alpha=1/3 + structural derivation), CKM angles (zero-import end-to-end via taste-staircase), neutrino mixing (PMNS via graph-first cycle structure), etc. The SM has ~19 free parameters; the framework reduces this to ~1 (S) after the substrate-derivable structure is accounted for. This is the framework's strongest publication-grade claim.

hypercharge_identification_note.label: Y0
hypercharge_identification_note.statement: absolute hypercharge normalization (alpha=1/3); the retained structure fixes ratios, while the overall Y-scale is a Y <-> g' rescaling convention with no physical content by itself
hypercharge_identification_note.basis: koide_y_substrate_anomaly_forcing_note_2026-05-08_probey_substrate_anomaly (retained_bounded): anomaly fixes ratios not absolute normalization

g_bare_rigidity_theorem_note.label: g0
g_bare_rigidity_theorem_note.class: vacuous rescaling convention (g <-> beta gauge choice)
g_bare_rigidity_theorem_note.basis: beta_gbare_rescaling_abstract_identity_narrow_theorem_note_2026-05-10 (retained): g_bare is rescaling-invariant convention, not a number to derive
